I farm 9.2 mu with only two people in the household, so I will keep the plan practical and labor I know I can finish myself. Because I have 20 years of experience and well irrigation, I will rely on crops that are familiar, stable, and easy for me to manage with timely water and fertilizer instead of making the plan too complicated. I will put more land into cabbage and Chinese cabbage because they fit my usual cropping habit and sell in volume, keep spinach as an early quick crop, and use smaller areas for chili, eggplant, and kidney bean so I still have cash crops but do not overload labor at peak time. I will use mostly hybrid seed for the vegetable crops where yield matters most, keep fertilizer moderate to strong for the heavy-feeding crops, irrigate more often for leafy vegetables and fruiting vegetables, and use rotary tillage because it is faster and suits my scale. My goal is steady yield, manageable field work, and lower risk across the year.
